title: How to Become a Freelancer
summary: Become a freelancer in 4 steps. Ontop shows you how to build your portfolio, land clients, and set up automated contracts and payments.
body_markdown:
Embarking on a freelance career often means juggling client outreach, portfolio building, contract setup, and payment management. Early challenges, such as setting competitive rates and landing that first paid job, can be overcome with practical guidance on pricing strategies and contract essentials. Clear direction on these matters simplifies the transition to a more flexible work life.


Freelancers benefit from systems that streamline tax matters, client payments, and compliance tasks, allowing them to focus on growing their business. Practical insights into managing proposals, portfolios, and invoices can pave the way to a successful independent career. Ontop’s[payroll software](https://www.getontop.com/) provides tools to handle payments and compliance efficiently, so freelancers can concentrate on winning new projects.


## Summary


- Freelancing is now a mainstream career path: 36% of the U.S. workforce was estimated to be freelancers in 2023, and 59 million Americans freelanced in the past year, creating greater competition and a stronger need for clear specialization.
- Many freelancers start with ad hoc tools that scale poorly, while 80% of organizations have automated payment processes, highlighting a gap that makes cross-border invoices and tax questions time-consuming.
- Clarity in your offer pays off: 50% of salespeople report struggling to identify the right skills to sell, and 70% of top sellers excel at naming and applying one core skill, showing that a one-sentence outcome boosts conversion.
- A concise, outcome-focused portfolio matters: 85% of hiring managers consider an online portfolio crucial, and 60% of professionals report receiving more job offers after creating one. Single-screen case studies win attention.
- Early client acquisition favors channels you can measure. Over 70% of freelancers find their first clients through online platforms, and 60% of small businesses acquire their first clients through social media. Test marketplaces, outreach, and content in parallel.
- Formal contracts and automated invoicing reduce friction and costs, as companies that automate contract management save an average of 30% on processing costs, and automated payment flows are already common in 80% of organizations.
- This is where[Ontop's payroll software](https://www.getontop.com/) fits in: it automates compliant contract management, tax classification, and cross-border payouts, reducing payment delays and administrative overhead.


## Why More People Want to Become Freelancers


‍


Freelancing has become a popular choice over traditional jobs because it[gives you control over who you work with](https://www.remofirst.com/post/remote-work-fueling-freelancer-boom) , when you work, and how you charge for your time. It also lets you connect with clients worldwide.


People choose freelance work when the benefits of independence and higher-value, project-based work outweigh the challenges of running a *one-person business* . Additionally, to manage your earnings effectively, consider how our[payroll software](https://www.getontop.com/) can streamline your billing and payment processes.


### What do people really want?


This trend is evident across marketing, design, and development: professionals want independence and flexibility, the ability to select projects that fit their skills, and the ability to travel or adjust their daily routines without losing income.


At first, this combination feels *liberating* , but then *raw responsibility* kicks in. When you choose your own hours, you also have to handle billing, contracts, taxes, and client relationships on your own.


### How has remote work changed opportunities?


In 2023, Freelancers Union reported that[36% of the U.S. workforce are freelancers](https://www.upwork.com/press/releases/new-upwork-study-finds-36-of-the-us-workforce-freelance-amid-the-covid-19-pandemic) . This shows that independent work is now a common career choice, not just an unusual option.


At the same time,[Upwork found that 59 million Americans](https://keywordseverywhere.com/blog/number-of-freelancers-stats/) freelanced in the past year. This indicates that many people view freelancing as either their primary or secondary source of income, underscoring the market's competitiveness.


The *practical effect* is clear: remote work has changed geography from a barrier into a resource, but it has also raised the standards for specialization, dependability, and clear payment agreements.


### Why do many freelancers stall before they scale?


Many people[manage cross-border contracts](https://www.getontop.com/blog/a-nova-realidade-dos-nomades-digitais-em-2024-redesenhando-o-trabalho-as-viagens-e-os-estilos-de-vida) , invoices, and payments with simple tools. This can seem easy and comfortable at first. However, as the number of clients increases and more countries are involved, problems can arise. Missing important details, getting paid late, and facing unexpected taxes can turn what seemed like freedom into a constant struggle.


[Platforms like Ontop](https://www.getontop.com/) help with this by automating the creation of compliant contracts, tax classification, and cross-border payments. This provides clear timelines and transparent fees, allowing independent workers to stop chasing money and start increasing their income.


### What separates the freelancers who thrive?


Treating freelancing like a **business** , not just a side job, makes all the difference. This approach involves establishing fixed systems for proposals, drafting clear contracts that define the scope of work and payment schedule, ensuring reliable invoicing, and planning for taxes and benefits.


When these parts are in place, relationships shift from one-time engagements to **ongoing retainer work** and referrals. This shift significantly reduces daily stress from uncertainty, enabling freelancers to think more strategically.


### What is the hardest piece to figure out?


The frustrating part is that this isn't even the hardest piece to figure out.


## Step One: Identify the Skill You Can Sell


‍


Name[one sellable service](https://www.getontop.com/blog/como-una-fintech-se-vuelve-rentable-la-historia-de-ontop-y-su-eficiencia-operativa-con-ia) that[produces a clear outcome](https://www.forbes.com/sites/matthewmottola/2024/06/25/the-freelance-economy-is-consolidating-heres-what-you-need-to-know) , then design everything around delivering that outcome consistently. Treat the skill like it’s a product: describe what you do, who you do it for, and what result they get, all in one short sentence that you could use during a sales call. For example, consider how effective[payroll software](https://www.getontop.com/) can streamline your processes and enhance client satisfaction.


### What do you already do that clients will *actually pay for* ?


Start by turning past tasks into **client outcomes** . Review three recent job descriptions, project summaries, or hobby activities to identify recurring actions, then rephrase each into a deliverable statement, such as"I write two 800-word blog posts that rank for niche keywords" or "I set up Shopify product pages and optimize checkout flows."


This activity helps shift the focus from tools to results. The pattern is common: people list tools, but clients are interested in results.[According to RAIN Group](https://www.rainsalestraining.com/blog/21-data-backed-sales-skills) , **half** of salespeople report difficulty identifying the right skills to sell, which explains why skilled beginners often get stuck at this point.


### How do you test the skill without overcommitting?


Run a single, time-limited experiment that you can finish in a week. Offer a paid trial with a clear focus or a fixed-price small offer, like one landing page, a two-hour support block, or one social media post package.


Treat the trial like a lab: write down how long each task actually takes, what inputs you need from clients, and the most common changes. These notes will become the basis for your delivery process and future estimates. This method reduces guesswork, makes pricing justifiable, and eases the worry of **what if they ask for more** .


### What does specificity look like in practice?


Choose a clear promise that you can explain in one sentence and give a single price. If you can't do that, you are[still selling confusion](https://www.getontop.com/blog/costos-de-desarrolladores-ee-uu-argentina) . The best way to check this is simple: describe your service in the time it takes to make a cup of coffee. If the listener asks, "What exactly do I get?" you are not clear enough.


The main danger here is offering too many services, which can confuse customers and turn proposals into long, hard-to-read lists. Focusing on fewer offerings increases sales because a precise offer appears more **trustworthy** and **repeatable** .


### What separates the people who sell confidently from those who hesitate?


The difference is not talent; it is **clarity** and **discipline** . Seventy percent of top sellers are effective at identifying and applying their key sales skills,[according to the Top Seller Study](https://www.rainsalestraining.com/blog/21-data-backed-sales-skills) . This shows that being able to name and use a single core skill provides a consistent advantage. Think of it like a restaurant menu: one **signature dish** , served perfectly, will create repeat customers faster than a hundred average choices.


### What checklist can you use right now?


#### Quick checklist you can use right now


- Pick one outcome-focused service and write it as a single-sentence promise.
- Create a one-week paid pilot with fixed deliverables and timing.
- Time each task and turn the timings into a simple pricing model.
- Write an email template that explains exactly what the client receives and the acceptance criteria.


### What choices change how clients see and pay you?


That step may seem small at first, but it reveals the **important choices** that come next.


These choices can really change how clients see and pay you.

## Step Two: Build Your First Portfolio and Online Presence


‍


Build a concise,[discoverable portfolio](https://www.getontop.com/blog/employer-branding-latam-strategies) that shows a specific result. Every piece of marketing should focus on that proof and include a clear way for clients to pay you. Start with one focused project page, one service page that explains the outcome you offer, and a single, clear call to action so clients know exactly what to do next, such as utilizing our payroll software for smooth transaction processing.


### What should a single project entry contain?


Start with the result, not the tools. Begin each project with a **one-sentence outcome** ; for example, "[reduced ecommerce checkout abandonment](https://thegood.com/insights/shopping-cart-abandonment) by 18 percent in four weeks."


Then, describe the problem you solved, explain the *exact steps* you took, and show the measurable outcome or how the client reacted. Add a visual or a short GIF that shows what you delivered, a downloadable one-page brief, and, if you have it, a client quote or acceptance email. Keep each entry on a single screen on mobile so potential buyers can see proof and next steps without scrolling.


### Which platform gets you the fastest traction?


If time and budget are limited, choose one platform where your clients already go and keep a single primary link. Marketplaces offer quick job flow and visibility. A simple personal page on Carrd, Notion, or GitHub Pages gives you a permanent, shareable home you control.


For long-term brand buyers, register a domain and focus on having a clear title tag and meta description. This helps ensure that search and referral links go to a page that converts.


**Recruiters** and **hiring managers** pay close attention to portfolios;[according to Knapsack Creative, 85% of hiring managers](https://knapsackcreative.com/blog-industry/guide-to-digital-presence) consider an online portfolio an important factor in evaluating candidates. Make that first impression count, especially if you're considering payroll software to improve your hiring processes.


### How do you show credibility before you have paid clients?


This is where **editing is more important than quantity** . Turn relevant tasks, class projects, or volunteer work into short case studies that show a clear method. Use the Problem, Approach, Outcome template and add a short bullet list titled "What you can expect" that aligns with what you promise in your service. If you have limited time, create a single public mini-project and track time spent and deliverables. Specific *details* and timestamps make a sample feel real.


This pattern is common among students and part-timers: when time is short, they often get stuck trying to perfect every item. Instead, they should spend that time on a single well-defined sample that demonstrates the exact result they offer.


### What small copy and layout changes increase conversions?


Put your promise in the **headline** , not buried in a paragraph. Replace 'Services' with a simple phrase that shows the outcome, and list exactly what the client gets in the **first three bullets** , such as delivery time and revision limits.


State a starter price or a *from* price so buyers can self-qualify; when the price is missing, many potential clients drop out. Include a prominent payment option and a brief statement on tax or compliance expectations so buyers know there are no surprises.


Simple microcopy like 'Fixed price, one-week delivery, unlimited email support for 48 hours' removes the guesswork that kills early deals.


Also, publishing **clear, printable terms** , a[document builds trust](https://www.getontop.com/blog/guia-de-leis-trabalhistas-da-espanha) , is **faster** than a long FAQ.


### How do you keep costs low and move fast?


Reuse, don’t remake. Turn a sample into a LinkedIn post, a one-page PDF, and a short video clip. *Use* free hosting and templates, compress images, and keep your site to two or three pages. Set aside two focused evenings for the launch work: one for building the page and another for creating and sharing the sample pieces across two channels.


When resources are tight, focus on **reach** and **clarity** rather than design perfection; a clear, honest page will perform better than an expensive site that looks nice but confuses buyers.


### How can you create momentum to get paid predictably?


Creating momentum to get paid reliably can lead to **increased offers** . According to a report by Knapsack Creative,[60% of professionals have received more job offers](https://knapsackcreative.com/blog-industry/guide-to-digital-presence) after creating an online portfolio.


### What happens after your portfolio setup?


While the setup may seem complete, **the real pressure** begins when you try to turn that proof into a paying client.


## Step Three: Find Your First Clients


‍


Mix channels, test quickly, and *treat each outreach as an*[experiment you can measure and repeat](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/grahamkelleynelson_i-dont-know-who-needs-to-hear-it-but-heres-activity-7386073848083025920-dea0) .


Utilize marketplaces and job boards for steady opportunities. Focus on targeted cold outreach to[win higher-value clients](https://www.getontop.com/blog/hourly-rate-from-salary-calculation) . Our[payroll software](https://www.getontop.com/) can streamline your processes and help you manage client payroll efficiently.


Create social content to generate **inbound interest** , and continue iterating until one channel yields **predictable responses** .


### Where should you look first?


Online marketplaces and curated job boards help you get noticed quickly and create clear project paths. This is especially helpful when you need repeat assignments to gain momentum.[According to Freelancer Union](https://www.freelancersunion.org/resources/first-clients/) , over 70% of freelancers find their first clients through online platforms. This shows how valuable that visibility can be for beginners.


Treat these platforms as *lead funnels* , not final customers: qualify them, test a small offer, and then move the buyer off-platform to build a better relationship.


### How do you write outreach that actually gets replies?


This challenge is common among new freelancers: they send long, generic pitches and then wonder why responses stall. **Be precise** , not clever. Reference one specific action the prospect took and state the measurable outcome you will deliver in one clear sentence. Close with a simple, actionable request, such as, “Can I do a 2-hour paid audit next week?”


Follow up twice on different days, offering fresh value rather than guilt. The failure mode occurs when the focus is on volume without craft; a dozen targeted, personalized notes **outperform** 200 templated blasts.


### Can social media really bring paying clients?


Yes, when you combine consistent, outcome-focused posts with direct, brief outreach to engaged responders, social channels become a reliable way to acquire new clients. Research from Small Business Trends shows that[60% of small businesses got their first clients](https://landingi.com/social-media-marketing/small-businesses/#:~:text=Definition%2C%20Tips%20&%20Examples-,Social%20Media%20Marketing%20for%20Small%20Business:%20Definition%2C%20Tips%20&%20Examples,lasting%20growth%20for%20your%20business.&text=Social%20media%20marketing%20has%20changed,to%20help%20you%20grow%20online.) through social media.


This highlights the effectiveness of using content alongside direct contact. By sharing case snippets, short lessons, and a clear call to action, you will guide readers to a single, action-oriented link.


### What do you do when a lead raises legal, tax, or payment questions?


Many freelancers manage invoices and cross-border payments with familiar tools. While this method works at first, issues can arise when a client operates in multiple countries. Invoices may be delayed, tax statuses can be confusing, and payment timing can become a long negotiation. This can change what should be an easy win into **weeks of administrative trouble** .


[Platforms like Ontop](https://www.getontop.com/) bring together[compliant contracts](https://www.getontop.com/case-studies) , automate **tax classification** , and support cross-border payments via *instant* USD wallets and debit access in over 150 countries. This reduces confusion and expedites access to funds, allowing freelancers to keep their work moving rather than waiting for slow bank transfers.


### How should you convert a small job into repeat work?


Use the first paid engagement as a **measurement system** . Time every task, capture what the client needs, and deliver a concise, documented deliverable that directly connects to business impact. Then, present a one-sentence retainer proposal based on that measured work and a clear schedule. This approach removes guesswork, builds trust, and changes one-off projects into **predictable monthly income** .


### What role do referrals and events play now?


Networking still matters, but it works differently now. *First* , show a quick win, then ask for an introduction. At events, trade *concrete business cards instead of standard* business cards.


For example, say, “I can audit your landing page in two hours for X fee,” and follow up within 48 hours with a deliverable. This specific approach beats vague promises, effectively converting curiosity into contracts.


### How do you effectively manage different client acquisition methods?


Think of getting new clients like fishing: it’s better to have a few **well-tuned hooks** in different places instead of using one net thrown around everywhere. Try one hook for a week; see how many bites you get, and then use your resources on the spot that really catches fish.


If you're looking to streamline your operations, consider how[payroll software](https://www.getontop.com/solutions/global-contractor-payroll) can simplify client management.

The next snag, the one that turns a signed agreement into an unpredictable cash flow problem, is where the story truly tightens.

## Step Four: Set Up Payment and Contract Processes


‍


Create a single, enforceable system: one contract template, clear[nonnegotiable payment](https://www.getontop.com/blog/que-constituye-el-costo-de-un-empleado-mas-alla-del-salario) terms, and an automated invoicing routine tied to milestones and signatures.


This approach eliminates the need to trade time for uncertainty and ensures reliable payment.


### What should my contract always include?


This pattern shows up in creative and technical projects: a vague deliverable leads to endless back-and-forth. Your template must name deliverables with[acceptance criteria](https://bytescout.com/blog/work-legally-as-a-freelancer-usa.html) , list milestones and due dates, state currency and payment schedule, set limits for revisions and hourly rates for extras, assign IP and licensing, and include steps for termination and dispute resolution.


Use *plain language* , include one acceptance checklist per milestone, and require a signed contract before any work begins. Think of the contract as a runway, not a suggestion; without it, projects stall due to *vague expectations* .


### How do I stop scope creep without wrecking client relationships?


When quick change requests pile up, freelancers often feel tired and guilty. The main problem remains: the lack of a formal change-order process.


It's important to add a **short amendment clause** stating that any requests outside the acceptance checklist require a **written change order** . This should be priced as either a **fixed fee** or a time-and-materials rate, with a *minimum charge* . Providing a simple, *client-friendly* option can also be helpful; for example, a 2-hour paid adjustment for small requests, and a priced proposal for bigger ones.


Include a checkbox acceptance so that everyone can easily sign off. Use *one-line scripts* for faster responses. For instance, you can say, “I can do that in a two-hour update for $X, ready to start once you approve.”


This method maintains good relationships and ensures you are paid for your time. Managing these workflows can be streamlined with **our**[payroll software](https://www.getontop.com/) to ensure everything is in order.


### Which payment methods should I offer?


When clients are based in the same country, **bank transfers** and card payments work well. For **global operations** , it's important to first show a preferred low-fee method, followed by other options.


Including a clear currency clause is necessary; for example, saying, “Fees quoted in USD, payer covers conversion costs,” makes it clear who is responsible for transaction fees and chargebacks.


It is a good idea to provide at least one instant payment option and a low-fee method for bank-to-bank settlements. Presenting choices this way **reduces negotiation time** and helps avoid unexpected deductions during reconciliation.


### How do I automate invoices and follow-ups?


Manual invoices are a slow leak that adds up over time. Use invoicing or accounting software to create **standard invoices** , send them regularly, set up **automatic reminders** , and get signatures or receipts for payments. Keep contract signatures and invoicing in one place so you can link each invoice to the specific milestone it covers.


In practice, **automated workflows** reduce hassle because[Pipefy Blog reports that 80% of organizations](https://www.pipefy.com/blog/procure-to-pay/) have automated their payment processes. If you make contracts and signature processes official, **processing costs** go down, too, as Pipefy Blog finds companies[save an average of 30% on processing costs](https://www.pipefy.com/blog/procure-to-pay/) by automating contract management.


### What do I do about international clients and taxes?


When a client is in a different jurisdiction, it is important to include a brief clause specifying who handles local taxes and whether the payment will be grossed up for withholding. **Require completed tax forms** before final payment, and use milestone payments to limit exposure. For large cross-border projects, it is advisable to require an upfront deposit, typically 20%-50%, and to structure the remaining balance into tied milestones.


Finally, keep simple, export-friendly language for intellectual property and deliverables. This helps avoid repeated negotiations over cross-border usage rights.


### What should I include in my practical checklist?


- Draft one **concise contract template** that includes an acceptance checklist and a change-order clause.
- Establish a nonnegotiable payment schedule that specifies a deposit percentage and a late fee.
- Select one **preferred payment method** and two backup options, ensuring fees are clearly stated.
- Automate invoice and reminder processing, linking each invoice to its corresponding contract milestone.
- Require a signed acceptance before releasing any work or files.


### Final thoughts on cash flow challenges?


That structure helps tackle most problems before they happen. But the next challenge quietly erodes *weeks of cash flow* .
